FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Wood and 
Other Lignocellulosic Products Sectional Committee had been approved by the Civil Engineering Division 
Council. 


Flattened bamboo board is manufactured from flattened bamboo as a core and/or with a combination of bamboo 
mat or veneer similar to plywood construction. Either bamboo mat or veneer can be used as cross bands and for 
face layer. 


In the present scenario, where availability of conventional timber has reduced to considerable extent this flattened 
bamboo board is expected to find extensive use. This standard bas been formulated to guide manufacturing of 
flattened bamboo boards specially used for weather exposed surface of building components in buildings and for 
decorative purposes. 


In the formulation of this standard, considerable assistance has been rendered by Indian Plywood Industries 
Research and Training Institute, Bengaluru. 


A scheme of labelling environment friendly products known as ECO-Mark has been instituted at the instance of 
the Ministry of Environment, Forests and Climate Change, Government of India. The ECO-Mark is administered 
by the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 as per the Resolution 
No.71 dated 21 February 1991 and Resolution No. 425 dated 20 October 1992 published in the Gazette of 
the Government of India. For a product to be eligible for ECO-Mark, it shall also carry the Standard Mark 
(ISI mark) of BIS besides meeting additional environment friendly requirements. For this purpose, the Standard 
Mark of BIS would be a single mark being a combination of the ISI Mark and the Eco logo. Requirements to be 
satisfied for a product to qualify for the BIS Standard Mark for Eco friendliness, will be optional. Manufacturing 
units will be free to opt for ISI Mark alone also. 


The ECO-Mark criteria is based on the Gazette Notification No. 170 dated 16 May 1996 for wood substitutes as 
environment friendly products published in the Gazette of Government of India, as revised/amended from time to 
time, as revised/amended from time to time. 


The Committee responsible for the preparation of this standard is given at Annex B. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test of analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS 2 : 1960 ‘Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised )’. The number of significant places retained in the 
rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 17571 : 2021 


Indian Standard 
FLATTENED BAMBOO BOARD — SPECIFICATION 


1 SCOPE 


This standard covers the requirements of flattened 
bamboo board used for weather exposed surface of 
building components and for decorative purposes.

possibility of applying the most recent editions of the

3 TERMINOLOGY 


For the purpose of this standard, the definitions given 
in IS 707 and IS 6874, and the following shall apply. 


3.1 Flattened Bamboo Board — Flattened bamboo 
board is manufactured from flattened bamboo as a core 
and/or with a combination of bamboo mat or veneer 
similar to plywood construction. Either bamboo mat or 
veneer can beused as cross bands and for face layer. 


3.2 Delamination — Inter-sliver separation within 
the mats or between the mats/veneer/flattened bamboo 
or between the flattened bamboos due to failure of 
adhesive bonding. 


4 MATERIALS 


4.1 Bamboo — Any suitable species of bamboo 
may be used for making flattened bamboo board. For 
ECO-Mark, bamboo mats shall be made from bamboo 
from sources other than natural forests. 


4.2 Veneer — Any species of timber may be used for 
manufacture of veneers. For ECO-Mark, only species 
of wood from other than natural forests, shall be used 
for the manufacture. 


4.3 Adhesive 


Adhesive for bonding flattened bamboos shall be of 
phenolic type conforming to BWP grade specified in 
IS 848. For the outermost layers of flattened bamboo 
board, resin admixed with suitable filler may be used to 
enhance the durability. 


5 MANUFACTURE 


5.1 Flattened Bamboo 


Flattened bamboo strips are thick uniform flat halves 
of bamboo processed from bamboo culm and made by 
either flattening the whole bamboo longitudinally after 
opening it by making a longitudinal cut or in case of 
hard and/or thick bamboo by splitting it longitudinally 
in two parts. 


IS 17571 : 2021 


5.2 Preservative Treatment 


5.2.1 Flattened bamboos shall be boiled for nearly 
4 h and then air dried for 2 to 4 days and finally dried 
to around 6 to 8 percent moisture content in a drying 
chamber. The flattened bamboos shall be subjected 
to 3 percent of boric acid equivalent (BAE) solution. 
Treatment of flattened bamboo shall be carried out after 
internal knot removal and flattening to avoid warping 
of flattened bamboo during drying cycle. 


5.2.2 Preservative treatment (glue line) of 
veneer/bamboo mat shall be given by incorporating the 
suitable preservatives like sodium pentachlorophenate 
or boron (octoborate or tetraborate) or any other 
suitable preservative chemical into the resin before 
adhesive application to protect against biodegradation. 


5.3 Application of Adhesive 


Adhesive shall be applied by soaking the flattened 
bamboos in the adhesive as mentioned in 4.3. 


5.4 Conditioning of Adhesive Coated Flattened 
Bamboos 


Adhesive coated flattened bamboo shall either be 
allowed sufficient length of open assembly time 
and passed through a band dryer or dried in a drying 
chamber at a temperature of (85+5) °C to bring down 
the moisture content of adhesive coated flattened 
bamboos to (12+2) percent. 


5.5 Assembly 


Depending on the thickness of flattened bamboos, 
adhesive coated and conditioned flattened bamboos as 
a core along with either wood veneers or bamboo mats 
placed as cross-bands/face layers, shall be placed on a 
rigid caul plate with biaxially oriented polypropylene 
(BOPP) film or any other similar material on both 
sides of the assembly as releasing agent. The assembly 
shall be of flattened bamboo as a core and a balanced 
construction with a combination of bamboo mat and/or 
veneer similar to plywood construction. Either bamboo 
mat or veneer can be used as cross-bands and for face 
layer. 


5.6 Hot Pressing 
Assembly of flattened bamboos shall be hot 
pressed at 140 °C to 145 °C at a specific pressure of 


1.6 N/mm? to 1.8 N/mm’. Hot pressing time shall 
depend on the thickness of the board. 


5.7 Moisture Content 


After hot pressing the finished flattened bamboo board 
shall be conditioned to moisture content not less than 
5 percent and not more than 15 percent. 


6 DIMENSIONS AND TOLERANCE 


6.1 When tested in accordance with IS 2380 (Part 2), 
the dimensions of flattened bamboo board shall be as 
follows: 


2440 mm x 1220 mm, 1840 mm x 1220 mm, 
2140 mm x 1220 mm, 1840 mm x 920 mm, 


2140 mm x 920 mm 


NOTE — The first dimension shall represent the length and the 
second width. 


6.2 Thickness 


The thickness shall be 3 mm, 4 mm, 6 mm, 9 mm, 
12 mm, 16 mm and 19 mm. 


NOTE — Any other dimensions (length, width and thickness) 
as agreed to between the manufacturer and the purchaser may 
also be used. 


6.3 Tolerances 


Tolerance on the nominal sizes of finished flattened 
bamboo board shall be as given in Table 1. 


Table 1 Tolerances on Nominal Sizes of Flattened 
Bamboo Board 


( Clause 6.3 )

Edge straightness and squareness shall be tested as per 
Annex A. 


7 WORKMANSHIP AND FINISH 


The flattened bamboo board shall be of uniform 
thickness within the tolerance limit specified in 6.3. 
The surface shall be reasonably smooth and uniform 
in colour.

8.2 Three number of test specimens shall be taken for 
each test, except flammability, flame penetration and 
rate of burning, for which six number of test specimens 
shall be taken for each of the test.

2 Three test specimens from each direction (both lengthwise and width-wise) for MOR and MOE from each sample of dimension as 


specified in IS 1734 (Part 11) shall be prepared. 


3 Three test specimens of size 200 mm x 100 mm of the give thickness shall be prepared from each sample and kept at hot air oven 


at (70 + 2) °C for 168 h followed by cooling at (27 + 2) °C for 3 h. The specimens shall then examined. 


4 Three test specimens of size 200 x 100 mm of the give thickness shall be prepared from each sample and subjected to seven cycles 


successively, each cycle consisting of the following operations: 


a) Specimen kept in hot air oven at (70 + 2) °C for 8 h. 
b) Immersed in cold water at (27 + 2) °C for 16 h. 


After completion of seven cycles, the specimens shall be dried in folds of blotting paper and then examined. 


5 Flammability is measured as the time taken for second ignition. Continuous flame on the second specimen for 1 min shall be 


considered as second ignition. 


6 t = thickness of specimen in mm. 


7 Time taken to lose weight from 30 percent to 70 percent.

9 SAMPLING AND 
CONFORMITY 


CRITERIA FOR 


The method of drawing representative sample and the 
criteria for conformity shall be as prescribed in IS 7638 
corresponding to AQL 1.5. 


10 ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS FOR 
ECO-MARK 


10.1 General Requirements 


10.1.1 The flattened bamboo board shall conform to the 
requirements of quality and performance as specified in 
this standard. 


10.1.2 The manufacturer shall produce to Bureau 
of Indian Standards, the environmental consent 
clearance from State Pollution Control Board as per 
the provisions of the Water (Prevention and Control 
of Pollution) Act, 1974 and Air (Prevention and 
Control of Pollution) Act, 1981, Water (Prevention 
and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981 and Water 
(Prevention and Control or Pollution) Cess Act, 1977 
along with the authorization, if required under the 
Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, while applying for 
ECO-Mark appropriate with enforced rules and 
regulations of Forest Department. 


10.2 Specific Requirements 
The flattened bamboo boardshall conform to the 


specific requirements given for ECO-Mark under 
relevant clause of the standard. 
NOTE — The manufacturer shall provide documentary 


evidence by way of certificate or declaration to Bureau of 
Indian Standards while applying for ECO-Mark. 


11 MARKING 


11.1 Each flattened bamboo boardshall be legibly 
and indelibly marked or stamped with the following 
particulars: 


a) Manufacturer’s name, his initials or his 
recognized trade mark, if any; 

b) Nominal dimensions (length, width and 
thickness); 


c) Date of manufacture; 
d) Batch number; and 


e) The criteria for which the flattened bamboo 
boardhas been labelled as ECO-Mark (in case 
the board has been marked with ECO-Mark) 
(see Foreword). 


11.2 BIS Certification Marking 


The product(s) conforming to the requirements of 
this standard may be certified as per the conformity 
assessment schemes under the provisions of the 
Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 and the Rules 
and Regulations framed thereunder, and the products 
may be marked with the Standard Mark. 


IS 17571 : 2021 


ANNEX A 
( Clause 6.3 ) 
METHOD OF TEST FOR EDGE STRAIGHTNESS AND SQARENESS 


A-1 PROCEDURE 
STRAIGHTNESS 


FOR EDGE 


The straightness of the edges and of flattened bamboo 
board shall be verified against a straight edge not less 
than the full length of the flattened bamboo board. If 
the edge on the end of the flattened bamboo board is 
convex. It shall be held against the straight edge in 
such a way as to give approximately equal gap at each 


end. The largest gap between the straight edge and the 
edge shall be measured to the nearest millimetre and 
recorded. 


A-2 PROCEDURE FOR SQUARENESS 


The squareness of flattened bamboo board shall be 
checked with a 1 200 mm x 1 200 mm square, by 
applying one arm of the square to the flattened bamboo 
board. The maximum width of the gap shall be recorded. 


IS 17571 : 2021

Bureau of Indian Standards 


BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 to promote harmonious 
development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to 
connected matters in the country. 


Copyright 


BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form without 
the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the 
standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to 
copyright be addressed to the Director (Publications), BIS. 


Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of 
‘BIS Catalogue’ and ‘Standards: Monthly Additions’. 


This Indian Standard has been developed from Doc No.: CED 20 (15037).
